newsitem.title: UK: LME copper sags again in late London.
newsitem.headline: LME copper sags again in late London.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices lurched lower on Thursday in late inter-office activity but edged up off a new two-month low at $1,840. Brokers cited Comex-led technical selling.
Earlier LME trading had seen Wednesday's break below $1,900 followed by fresh technical sales and liquidation. Traders expected a test $1,825 and $1,800.
Final three months business was at $1,852 a tonne, $63 down from Wednesday.
After the post-kerb drop copper was bid at 1900 GMT when Comex closed back up at $1,850.

Brokerage Rudolf Wolff's Evening Metal Report said some support may emerge if LME stocks register another fall on Friday but, with technical indicators trending down, it also looks for new tests of underlying support.
Aluminium was bid late at $1,434 and just above the day's new two-year low at $1,429.
